findings.title: Gates 3.2a and 3.7 cannot pass while tests of removed behaviour still exist
findings.description:
Task 3.2a requires `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test` to pass right after 3.1–3.2 stop rendering `Comprehension:` and `### Adoption Facts`. Two core tests still assert that output at that point:
- **`pipeline-integration.test.ts:184`** expects `Comprehension: …`, and lines 154–173 expect probe facts in the prompt. This block is only deleted in 3.3.
- **`adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts:99-103`** (`expectBrownfield`) expects the `### Adoption Facts` heading. This file is only deleted in 4.1.

Task 3.7 requires `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm -r test` to pass, and has the same problem. `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts:68` still calls `createContextPipeline(dir, { adoptionStateWrites, squadronProbe })`, and its brownfield cases expect the swap that 3.3 removed.

A junior implementer following the file literally hits a red gate with no instruction, or deletes tests out of order.

Fix:
- Move the `pipeline-integration.test.ts` brownfield block deletion from 3.3 into 3.1/3.2.
- Move the `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` deletion from 4.1 to before 3.2a.
- State in 3.2a that `ContextIntegrator.test.ts` and `adoptionParity.test.ts` are unaffected at that point: the first uses a mock engine, the second is outside the core package.

findings.title: Commit points are written as checkboxes, not `**Commit**:` marker lines
findings.description:
Commits appear as checkbox tasks or sub-items at 2.3 (line 79), 3.2a (101), 3.7 (134), 4.1–4.4 (148, 155, 163, 169), 5.1 (186) and 6.3 (206). The convention is a plain `**Commit**: …` line, never a checkbox, so the implementer and task-checker recognise it as a marker and not as work to tick off.

The placement is sound: each sits at a compiling, tested point once the FAIL above is fixed. Convert them to plain marker lines and fold 2.3 and 3.2a into the preceding task.

findings.title: Check 6.2 says "prints nothing" but names an expected hit
findings.description: The grep includes `fileComprehension`, which will match the retained `COMPREHENSION_PROFILE_VARIABLE = 'fileComprehension'` at `packages/core/src/detection/comprehensionAnalysis.ts:15`. The exception is stated, but the success line "all three checks are clean" reads as a contradiction. Say "prints only that line".
